title: Heat-health action plan activation, thresholds and emergency care: a narrative review for decision-makers
abstract: Aim: to summarise evidence on heat-health plan activation and emergency department visits, the effect of lowering activation thresholds, equity effects and activation costs. Design: narrative review with stated certainty for each finding. Results will follow the search and synthesis.
introduction: Heat-health action plans are widely used, but their effects on emergency care, the value of lower thresholds and who benefits are uncertain.
methods: Searches of three databases and agency websites; structured extraction; synthesis by question with certainty stated in words; costs described without combining them with effects.
results: No data have been collected yet.
discussion: The discussion will set out what the board can and cannot conclude and what local monitoring would add.
limitations: Observational evidence; narrative synthesis; one main reviewer.
summary: Narrative review structure with results left empty.
